items.title: Dwelling in Observation of the Body

items.zh: 住循身觀略有三種。謂依身增上聞思修慧。由此慧故，於一切身、一切相，正觀察、正推求、隨觀隨覺。
items.en: Dwelling in observation of the body is, briefly, of three kinds: wisdom born of hearing, of reflection, and of cultivation, each arising in dependence on the body's own capacity. Through this wisdom, one correctly observes and correctly investigates every body and every aspect of it, observing and thereby awakening to its true nature accordingly.

items.title: The Threefold Pattern Across Body, Feeling, Mind, and Phenomena; What Is Mindfulness

items.zh: 念，謂依身增上，受持正法，思惟法義，修習作證，於文、於義修作證中，心無忘失。
items.en: The body's three kinds are: intrinsic impurity, as in the body's interior parts; apparent purity, as in the body's skin; and the impurity of decay, as in the body's parts once turned livid after death. Feeling's three kinds are: painful, pleasant, and neutral feeling. Mind's three kinds are: mind associated with painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling respectively. Phenomena's three kinds are: dark, bright, and mixed dark-and-bright states. What is mindfulness? It is, in dependence on the body's own capacity, retaining the true teaching, reflecting on its meaning, and cultivating it to direct realisation — remaining, throughout engagement with both the letter and the meaning, and through to realisation, without any lapse of memory.

items.title: Section: The Establishment of Mindfulness — Two Complete Frameworks

items.zh: 若審思惟：我於正法為正受持，為不爾耶？於彼彼義慧善了達，為不爾耶？善能觸證彼彼解脫，為不爾耶？如是審諦安住其念，名為念住。又為守護念、為於境無染、為安住所緣，名為念住。為守護念者，謂如說言：先守護念，若常委念。為於境無染者，謂如說言：念守護心，行平等位，不取其相，不取隨好，廣說乃至守護意根，修意根律儀。為安住所緣者，謂如說言：於四所緣安住其念。謂於遍滿所緣、淨行所緣、善巧所緣、淨惑所緣。
items.en: If one carefully reflects: have I correctly retained the true teaching, or not? Have I, with wisdom, thoroughly understood its meaning, or not? Have I genuinely touched and realised liberation through it, or not? — abiding in mindfulness through such careful self-examination is called the establishment of mindfulness. Further: for the sake of guarding mindfulness, for the sake of remaining undefiled towards the object, and for the sake of abiding in the object — this too is called the establishment of mindfulness. Abiding in the object means, as has been said, abiding in mindfulness with respect to the four objects: the pervasive object, the purifying object, the skilful object, and the object that purifies affliction.

items.zh: 由此三相，善住其念，故名念住。

云何為受？謂樂受、苦受、不苦不樂受。樂身受、苦身受、不苦不樂身受。如說身受，心受亦爾。樂有愛味受、苦有愛味受、不苦不樂有愛味受。無愛味受、依耽嗜受，當知亦爾。樂依出離受、苦依出離受、不苦不樂依出離受。如是總有二十一受，或九種受。云何為心？謂有貪心、離貪心、有瞋心、離瞋心、有癡心、離癡心、略心、散心、下心、舉心、掉心、不掉心、寂靜心、不寂靜心、定心、不定心、善修心、不善修心、善解脫心、不善解脫心。如是總有二十種心。云何為法？謂若貪、貪毘奈耶法，若瞋、瞋毘奈耶法，若癡、癡毘奈耶法，若略、若散法，若下、若舉法，若掉、不掉法，若寂靜、不寂靜法，若定、不定法，若善修、不善修法，若善解脫、不善解脫法。如是當知建立黑品、白品、染品、淨品二十種法。
items.en: What is feeling? Pleasant, painful, and neutral feeling … each of these three, whether craving-tinged, free of craving, bound up with indulgence, or bound up with genuine release — twenty-one kinds of feeling in all, or nine in brief. What is mind? A mind with desire, or free of desire … a well-liberated mind, or one not yet liberated — twenty kinds of mind in all. What is phenomena? Whatever pertains to desire, or to the discipline that ends desire … whatever pertains to being well-liberated, or not yet liberated — establishing, in this way, twenty states classed as dark, bright, defiled, and pure.

items.zh: 又樂受者，謂順樂受觸為緣所生平等受，受所攝，是名樂受。此若五識相應，名身受；若意識相應，名心受。如順樂受觸，如是順苦受觸、順不苦不樂受觸為緣所生不平等受，受所攝，非平等非不平等受，受所攝，是名苦受、不苦不樂受。此若五識相應，名身受；若意識相應，名心受。

items.title: Feeling's Four Kinds Explained; Mind Sorted by Activity and by Sitting

items.zh: 如是諸受，若隨順涅槃、隨順決擇，畢竟出離、畢竟離垢、畢竟能令梵行圓滿，名無愛味受。若墮於界，名有愛味受。若色無色界繫，若隨順離欲，名依出離受。若欲界繫，若不順離欲，名依耽嗜受。又有貪心者，謂於可愛所緣境事，貪纏所纏。離貪心者，謂即遠離如是貪纏。有瞋心者，謂於可憎所緣境事，瞋纏所纏。離瞋心者，謂即遠離如是瞋纏。有癡心者，謂於可愚所緣境事，癡纏所纏。離癡心者，謂即遠離如是癡纏。如是六心，當知皆是行時所起三煩惱品，及此三品對治差別。略心者，謂由正行，於內所緣繫縛其心。散心者，謂於外五妙欲隨順流散。下心者，謂惛沈睡眠俱行。舉心者，謂於淨妙所緣明了顯現。掉心者，謂大舉故，掉纏所掉。
items.en: Among these feelings: whatever accords with nirvana, accords with discernment, and finally brings about departure, purity, and the fulfilment of the holy life, is called feeling free of craving. Whatever falls within the three realms is called feeling tinged with craving. Whatever belongs to the form or formless realm, or accords with dispassion, is called feeling bound up with transcendence. Whatever belongs to the desire realm and does not accord with dispassion is called feeling bound up with indulgence. A mind with desire is one bound by the fetter of desire towards an attractive object; a mind free of desire has simply left that fetter behind — and likewise for aversion and delusion. These six minds, occurring during ordinary activity, are the three afflictions and their three respective antidotes. A contracted mind is one bound, through calm-abiding practice, to a single inner object. A scattered mind is one following the outward flow of the five sense pleasures. A sunken mind is one accompanied by dullness and drowsiness. A lifted mind is one in which a pure and excellent object appears vividly. An agitated mind is one so over-lifted that it is caught by the fetter of restlessness.

blocks.text: How one "dwells observing" body, feeling, and mind. A short passage (0440b23) is untranslated.

"Of three kinds: wisdom born of hearing, of reflection, and of cultivation, each arising in dependence on the body." Venerable Miào Jìng: it is the higher teaching the Buddha expounded on the basis of our own body.

The body is impure by nature (its inner parts), apparently pure (its skin), and impure in decay (the corpse). The same threefold pattern runs through feeling, mind, and phenomena. **Mindfulness** means "remaining, through the letter and the meaning, and through to realisation, without any lapse".

"If one carefully reflects: have I correctly retained the true teaching or not? Have I understood its meaning? Have I touched liberation?" Venerable Miào Jìng: "I don't need others to find my faults; I examine myself."

Pleasant, painful, neutral; of body or mind; "craving-tinged or free of craving, bound up with indulgence or with release". Venerable Miào Jìng: three by nature, two by basis, multiplied by four. "Whatever falls within the three realms is craving-tinged."

Feeling free of craving "accords with nirvāṇa". Mind is sorted into twenty states: with desire or free of it, with aversion, with delusion, contracted or scattered, sunken or lifted, and so on. Venerable Miào Jìng: "contracted" means the mind does not engage its object.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say "the body not included in the faculties" is?
options: the supporting sense-organ — outward, part of the body, but not the faculty itself, unable to produce the five consciousnesses
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it refers to the supporting sense-organ — outward, still part of the body, but not the faculty, and unable to give rise to the five consciousnesses.

quiz.q: The English renders 依身增上 as "in dependence on the body's own capacity." How do the masters read it?
options: Miào Jìng: the higher teaching the Buddha gave concerning the body; Cháng Bǎi: relying on a healthy, strong body that supports retaining the Dharma
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: it is the higher teaching the Buddha expounded on the basis of our body. Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on the body's health and strength helps the practitioner retain the Dharma and gain the wisdom of hearing. Their readings differ.

quiz.q: The text says mindfulness is "no lapse of memory in letter, meaning, and realisation." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say it is, more deeply?
quiz.why: "Remaining, throughout engagement with both the letter and the meaning, and through to realisation, without any lapse of memory." Venerable Miào Jìng: put more deeply, mindfulness is dhāraṇī — a matter of great importance.

quiz.q: What does the treatise call the establishment of mindfulness, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi match the three questions?
options: examining whether one has rightly retained, understood, and realised — abiding in mindfulness this way; the three questions match hearing, reflection, cultivation
quiz.why: "Abiding in mindfulness through such careful self-examination is called the establishment of mindfulness." Master Cháng Bǎi: retaining the Dharma matches the wisdom of hearing; understanding its meaning, reflection; touching liberation, cultivation.

quiz.q: "Have I rightly retained the teaching, or not?" What does Venerable Miào Jìng say this is?
options: no need for others' criticism — checking oneself whether one has accomplished it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: I don't need others to find fault with me; I examine myself — have I accomplished it or not?

quiz.q: Feeling numbers "twenty-one in all, or nine." What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: three by nature, two by basis (body, mind), four by distinction — nine; Cháng Bǎi: even painful feeling can be craving-tinged when one clings to it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: feeling has three by its own character and two by basis — body and mind — making five; add four distinctions and you get nine. Master Cháng Bǎi: some people cling to painful feeling; even pain can be a craving-tinged feeling when one is attached to it.

quiz.q: What is craving-tinged feeling, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "falls"?
options: whatever falls within the realms; 墮 means entering — inside the three realms with no way out
quiz.why: "Whatever falls within the three realms is called feeling tinged with craving." Venerable Miào Jìng: 墮 means "enters" — entering the desire, form, or formless realm, you cannot get out of that range.
